label: copy-phase input p at recall positions 1-2 (p fed back as orig token 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input is the letter p at recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the model has just emitted p as original token 0 (step L+1) or original token 1 (step L+2). Magnitude depends on position: when p is the first original token (input p right after <DEL>), activation is strong (~0.85-1.0 of max, 83% of activation mass); when p is the second original token, activation is weak (~0.1-0.4 of max). Never fires during the original phase or the delimiter step, never on p at later copy positions (recall_idx >= 3), and essentially never on any other token. Most false positives are p at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L = 3-4) where the feature stays silent.

issues: Every factual claim checks out on the profile: activation is 100% in the copy phase and zero in the original and delimiter phases. 99.99% of activation mass sits on in_tok p. recall_idx 1 holds 82.9% of the mass and recall_idx 2 holds 17.1%. There is 1 activation at recall_idx 3 and 2 on c (both tiny). The test split has only 1 missed activation (e at 0.01).

The false positives form one systematic class, which the explanation already mentions: p at recall_idx 2 in short sequences. At L=3 the feature is essentially silent (precision 0.007). At L=4 it is about 50/50 (precision 0.45). At L>=5 it is reliable (precision 0.998).

On test, excluding the L=3 case gives a slightly better predicate: F1 0.979 vs 0.972, recall 0.9999. Excluding L<=4 gives F1 0.982 but loses recall (0.965). Both gains are small, and the original predicate and label are fine.
